newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse ends firmer on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse ends firmer on foreign buying.

text.p: Most prices on the Bucharest stock exchange closed higher on Tuesday due to strong buying pressure from foreign investors, traders said.
"Foreign investors bought heavily in first tier stocks, mainly in pharmaceuticals and chemicals, but supply was thin," one trader said.
Closing prices of 26 stocks rose, eight went down and three ended flat, while five had no trade. On Monday two stocks were suspended.
Low supply pushed down total turnover to 17.02 billion lei from 22.1 billion in the previous session.
"I expect buying pressure to continue throughout the week as it appears that foreigners are determined to buy," one trader said.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, touched new all-time highs, rising by 2.6, 2.88 and 2.72 percent respectively from the previous session.

Traders said investors had focused on first tier chemical plant Oltchim, which closed 200 lei firmer at 4,200. They also said interest had been strong in pharmaceutical makers Antibiotice and Terapia. The stocks firmed by 350 and 1,050 lei to 8,450 and respectively 9,500.
First tier Azomures fertiliser maker was relatively stable on Tuesday, inching up 50 lei to 4,200.
Policolor dye maker, another first tier listing, gained 150 lei to close at 7,400. Refrigerator maker Arctic stayed suspended.
Buyers had started to show interest in some cheap second-tier stocks which had stayed idle over the past months, brokers said.
On the second tier, industrial fittings maker Armatura Cluj was in high demand and closed 900 lei firmer at 4,900, taking the bulk of the turnover on the tier.
The VAB index is displayed on VANGUARD. The CAS-SE is on CASE02.
